prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There’s no single “official” service that tells you whether every AI assistant (ChatGPT, Bing Chat, Bard, Siri, etc.) will recommend your business. The practical approach is to (A) make sure your business data is visible and optimized where those AIs get their signals (Google, Bing, Apple, websites), and (B) regularly test and monitor model responses yourself — manually or with simple automated checks. Below is a compact, actionable plan and the best services to use.

1) Make sure AIs can find and trust your business (most important)
- Google Business Profile (formerly GMB): Primary source for Google/Bard/Assistant recommendations. Claim and optimize.
- Bing Places: Important for Bing Chat / Microsoft Copilot.
- Apple Maps / Yelp / Facebook / industry directories: Other assistants and knowledge sources reference these.
- Structured data on your website: Add Schema.org LocalBusiness markup and FAQ/HowTo where relevant.

2) Services to manage presence and citations
- BrightLocal — local SEO, citation monitoring, rank tracking, review monitoring. Good for seeing presence across directories.
- Yext — centralized knowledge/profile management and push to many directories; analytics about where your info is used.
- Moz Local / Whitespark — citation cleanup and local ranking tools.
These increase the chance LLMs will surface or cite your business.

3) Tools to monitor whether you appear in search/answers (indirect proxy for LLM recommendations)
- SEMrush / Ahrefs / Moz — track keywords, featured snippets, and SERP presence (LLMs often pull from high-ranking pages/snippets).
- BrightLocal local rank tracker — checks local search placements regularly.

4) Direct testing against AI engines (recommended)
- Manual testing: periodically ask the popular assistants yourself with a set of prepared prompts (see sample prompts below).
- Automated testing: script queries against:
  - OpenAI API (ChatGPT-family models) to run repeatable prompts.
  - Bing Web Search API and Bing Chat (where available) for Microsoft.
  - Google Search API + Bard (Bard may not have a public API but you can test manually or via automated browser tests).
Capture and log responses to see if your business is recommended.

Sample test prompts (use variations):
- “I’m in [city/zip]. Recommend the top 5 [service/category] near me and explain why.”
- “Where should I go for [specific need] within [x miles of address/ZIP]?”
- “List the best [category] in [city], and include phone and address.”

5) How to interpret results and act
- If LLMs don’t recommend you but you appear in Google/Bing results: improve site SEO, reviews, local citations, and schema markup.
- If you don’t appear in directory results: fix citations via BrightLocal/Yext/Moz Local.
- Encourage positive reviews and get local backlinks; these are strong signals LLMs indirectly use.

6) Reality check
- LLM answers vary by model, prompt, and time; there’s no guaranteed “indexing” or “recommendation” registry for all AIs.
- Many LLMs use proprietary combinations of knowledge graph, web search, and training data — optimizing the sources above is your best lever.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a set of test prompts tailored to your business and location,
- Write a simple script (OpenAI API + scheduler) to run automated weekly checks and log results,
- Recommend the best mix of BrightLocal vs Yext for your business size and budget. Which would you prefer?
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
